adjudication_records.issue_text: CryptoIntegration.java:55 — Crypto providers with equal priority are selected unpredictably by ServiceLoader iteration order, allowing a non-FIPS provider to be chosen when multiple providers use priority 200 instead of failing safely.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that multiple providers with the same priority (200) will have unpredictable selection order. Looking at the diff, DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all return order() = 200, while AuthzClientCryptoProvider returns 100. The code at line 55 sorts by order().reversed() and takes the first one, but when orders are equal, the ServiceLoader iteration order determines selection. This is a legitimate design concern - in environments where multiple providers with priority 200 are on the classpath, the selection is non-deterministic. However, this appears to be intentional design (only one main crypto provider should be on classpath at a time), and the authz-client provider has lower priority (100) specifically to be overridden. This is a valid architectural concern but not a bug since the expected deployment has only one main provider.
